title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: Value at Risk in One Container
content:
Under `Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims`, the amount placed on a notice of loss is built on the commercial invoice value of the goods in a single container of the shipment.

## Definition

The **container value** is found from two records kept for the cover holder: the declared cargo value shown on the transport document of the booking under this cover, and the container count of that booking. The first is divided by the second and rounded to the cent.

Where either record is missing, or carries no value, the container value is instead the cover's insured value divided by the number of containers the cover takes, rounded to the cent.

## Condition, judgement, result

| Transport document value on record | Booking container count on record | Container value |
|---|---|---|
| present | present | declared cargo value divided by the booking's container count |
| missing or empty | any | cover's insured value divided by the cover's container count |
| any | missing or empty | cover's insured value divided by the cover's container count |

## Worked examples (hypothetical figures)

- Declared cargo value 250000.00 USD on the transport document; the booking has 3 containers. The container value is 83333.333, rounded to 83333.33 USD.
- No declared cargo value on record; the cover has an insured value of 90000.00 USD over 4 containers. The container value is 22500.00 USD.
